title: Op-variant Ledger: online autotuner for phase-aware kernel selection
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: The runtime currently picks kernel implementations based on static heuristics (arch + seqlen buckets) that don't adapt quickly to workload phase changes (mixed prefills, conversational bursts, variable batch shape). This ticket implements an online "op-variant ledger" — a lightweight empirical store + tuner that tracks per-op-variant performance by architecture, batch-size, seq-len bucket, and token-phase and uses that data to recommend/score kernel candidates at request time.

Goals: (1) reduce p95 latency tail for mixed conversational workloads by dynamically preferring kernels that empirically minimize tail latency under observed token-phase patterns; (2) limit cost regression by combining cheap microbench probes with conservative validation; (3) provide safe rollout and automatic fallback to baseline kernels on anomalies.

Approach summary: Build an Op-variant Ledger service that ingests microprobe results and warm-start telemetry (short synthetic prefill runs + selected live sampling). The ledger maintains exponentially-weighted aggregates for latency, throughput, and failure rates per (op_variant_id, hw_arch, seqlen_bucket, batch_range, token_phase). A small online tuner scores kernel candidates with a regret-regularized objective: score = latency_est * (1 + lambda * stderr) + gamma * cost_est + exploration_bonus. We will seed the ledger using offline microbench profiles and transfer warmstart profiles for similar models/archs. The runtime consults the ledger at scheduling time with a strict budget for lookup latency (<=250us) and may choose to run a microprobe in-band when uncertainty is high and latency budget allows.

Unique aspects vs prior autotuners: ensemble of (cheap microbench + streaming telemetry + transfer warmstarts), token-phase aware scoring, calibrated regret bands to avoid oscillation, and a lightweight safety net that prefers baseline kernel if failure or tail regresses beyond threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger service ingests microprobe+telemetry and persists EWMA metrics per op-variant and metadata keys
Runtime consults ledger and changes kernel choice for >= 10% of mixed conversational requests in canary traffic
p95 latency on mixed conversational benchmark reduced by >= 8% vs baseline without increasing p50 by >2%
Cost per token change <= 3% for the production profile or justified in release notes
Canary rollout with automatic rollback triggers (latency/cost/failure thresholds) implemented and tested
Dashboard shows per-op-variant heatmap, confidence bands, probe counts, and recent rollbacks
